entertainment.title: ‘Young Sheldon’ Star Emily Osment Requested Intimacy Coordinator Over Age Gap With Montana Jordan: “He Was a Baby!”
entertainment.summary: The actress, who was 30 when she joined the CBS series, recalled feeling "uncomfortable" about the age difference between her and her 18-year-old onscreen love interest.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Young Sheldon star Emily Osment recalls requesting an intimacy coordinator during her time on the CBS series because of the age gap between her and co-star Montana Jordan. Osment, who played Mandy McAllister, was 30 when she joined the series in 2022, while Jordan, who played George Cooper, was 18.

Revealed in Jessica Radloff’s new book, Young Sheldon: The (Juicier-Than-Meemaw’s-Brisket) Inside Story of the Hit Comedy , which is a behind-the-scenes oral history of the series, Osment explained that while she and Jordan didn’t share sex scenes, she felt “uncomfortable” because of their age difference. Related Stories TV Inside the Shocking Decision to End 'Young Sheldon' at Its Peak (Exclusive Excerpt) TV Valerie Mahaffey, Actress on 'Northern Exposure,' 'Desperate Housewives' and 'Young Sheldon,' Dies at 71

“That made me uncomfortable. He was a baby! A baby with a mullet,” Osment said. “So I spoke to Tim Marx, and obviously they were not able to get one that late in the day, but for the next few episodes they had one there, since the relationship between them escalates. It made everything easier having one there. I think it’s something that’s really important.”

“I don’t know if Montana even knew if he could ask for that. Like, let’s give him the option, too. Make him comfortable. And he’s such a sweet kid, I think he would just eat his discomfort,” she continued. “But I love those guys, and I’m really happy it got to the point where they were able to do that [for us].”

Elsewhere in the book, director Alex Reid acknowledged that production initially “dropped the ball” and overlooked having an intimacy coordinator, saying that the team’s decision was influenced by the show’s lack of sex scenes.

“I have a photo between takes of them sitting in that car when we shot that, and they’re looking off in other directions. I showed it to Emily and she said, ‘Yeah, that was so uncomfortable for both of us, because we didn’t know each other,’” Reid added. “It wasn’t even about the lack of an intimacy coordinator. It’s just you’re having to make out with somebody you just kind of met. Obviously they worked that out, and they have a great chemistry now, but that was kind of embarrassing.”

Now, Osment and Jordan star in the Young Sheldon spinoff Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage, which is in its third season and airs Thursdays at 8 p.m. ET on CBS.

entertainment.title: Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg & Too $hort Electrify Jay-Z30 Tour’s Final Stop
entertainment.summary: Night two at SoFi Stadium also paid tribute to Nipsey Hussle.
entertainment.body:
As many may have anticipated, Jay-Z didn’t formally announce whether he’ll be headlining 2027’s Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show during the final stop (Oct. 24) on his heralded JAY-Z30 Tour. Nevertheless, the hip-hop icon kept the packed audience inside Los Angeles’ (Inglewood) SoFi Stadium — host of next year’s NFL showdown — on its feet for two hours as he welcomed surprise guests and fellow genre pioneers Too $hort, Snoop Dogg and Dr. Dre during the proceedings.

Opening with “The Watcher 2,” Jay-Z smoothly segued into the hip-hop anthem “Blow the Whistle.” Then the crowd erupted into boisterous cheers and applause as Oakland, Calif.’s Too $hort arrived to lead a stadium-wide rap-along. From there — starting with “Izzo (H.O.V.A.)” — Jay-Z reeled off a string of classic singles and fan-fave album tracks including “Beach Is Better,” “Family Feud,” “Dirt Off Your Shoulder,” “Dead Presidents” and “D’Evil.” That run also featured the hit “Hard Knock Life.”

In honor of late rapper Nipsey Hussle, Jay-Z integrated elements of “Hussle & Motivate” into the former. He also performed “On to the Next One,” which featured the instrumental from Hussle’s “Last Time That I Checc’d.”

Taking a brief break at that point, Jay-Z turned the stage over to the evening’s two additional surprise guests: L.A’s own Snoop Dogg and Dr. Dre. The pair sparked another rollicking rap-along with renditions of “The Next Episode,” “California Love,” “Nothin’ But a ‘G’ Thang,” and “Still D.R.E.” Afterward, Jay-Z returned for a second half that featured “99 Problems,” “Excuse Me Miss,” “Jigga,” “Empire State of Mind” and “Ni**as in Paris” among other selections before closing with “Encore.”

Among the celebs attending Jay-Z30 night two were Kelly Rowland, Lizzo, DJ Khaled, Yo Gotti, B2K, Snoh Aalegra, Hit-Boy and Wizkid. On the first evening of his two-night, sold-out L.A. stand (Oct. 23), Jay-Z welcomed daughter Blue Ivy, John Legend, DJ Khaled and Scarface as his surprise guests.

These two shows were the culmination of a tour celebrating the 30 th anniversary of Jay-Z’s 1996 debut studio album Reasonable Doubt and the 25 th anniversary of his sixth studio album The Blueprint . Kicking off those celebrations with a three-night engagement at Yankee Stadium in July, Jay-Z took the party overseas to London and Paris in September before coming to L.A.

Further rounding out Jay-Z’s anniversary celebration thus far is the docuseries JAY-Z in 8 with legendary producer Rick Rubin. It’s currently airing on HBO Max. And now it’s wait and see if Jay-Z’s L.A. stand is the portent of things to come in regards to next year’s Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show.

entertainment.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love’ Returns to No. 1 on Billboard 200
entertainment.summary: Plus, Zach Bryan’s Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs debuts at No. 2.
entertainment.body:
Olivia Rodrigo ’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love returns to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart (dated Oct. 31) for a third nonconsecutive week on top. The set surges from the runner-up slot with a 15% gain in equivalent album units earned (75,000) in the United States in the week ending Oct. 22. The increase was largely spurred by the release of a new remix of the album’s latest single, “Expectations,” with Chappell Roan, on Oct. 15, alongside its official music video .

Rodrigo’s album spent its first two weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 (dated June 27 and July 4) and has yet to leave the weekly top five in its 19 weeks on the list.

Also in the top 10 of the latest Billboard 200, Zach Bryan ’s Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs debuts at No. 2, marking the singer-songwriter’s sixth top 10-charted project. The eight-song release, which includes collaborations with Lana Del Rey and Turnpike Troubadours, was announced on Oct. 12 and released four days later. It’s Bryan’s second release of the year, following the No. 1-debuting With Heaven on Top in January.

The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. The new Oct. 31, 2026-dated chart will be posted in full on Billboard ‘s website on Oct. 27. For all chart news, follow @billboard and @billboardcharts on both X, formerly known as Twitter, and Instagram.

Of you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love ’s 75,000 equivalent album units earned in the latest tracking week, SEA units comprise 63,000 (up 19%, equaling 67.14 million on-demand official streams of the set’s tracks; it moves 2-1 on Top Streaming Albums for a fifth total week in the lead), album sales comprise 11,000 (down 7%; it climbs 6-3 on Top Album Sales) and TEA units comprise 1,000 (up 121%).

Zach Bryan’s Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs launches at No. 2 on the latest Billboard 200 with 65,500 equivalent album units earned. Of that sum, SEA units comprise 59,500 (equaling 60.46 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs; it debuts at No. 2 on Top Streaming Albums), album sales comprise 5,000 (it was only available to purchase as a standard download album; it debuts at No. 15 on Top Album Sales) and TEA units comprise 1,000. The CD and vinyl editions of the album are due out in December.

entertainment.title: Miranda Lambert Headlining Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving Game Halftime Show
entertainment.summary: She'll take the AT&T Stadium stage at the Nov. 26 Cowboys-Eagles matchup.
entertainment.body:
Texas native Miranda Lambert is set to headline the Dallas Cowboys’ halftime show when the team plays the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day at AT&T Stadium.

The annual Cowboys halftime entertainment segment, officially titled the Salvation Army Red Kettle Kickoff Halftime Show, puts a spotlight on the needs of millions during the holiday season and beyond — with the Red Kettle Campaign raising more than $3.4 billion over the past three decades. Donations provide assistance to those in need in the community in which they’re given. Information about giving help or getting help is available at SalvationArmyUSA.org .

“It’s the 30th anniversary. You’ve gotta take the bull by the horns,” Lambert — who released her 10th solo studio album, Crisco , in early October — says in the promo spot seen below that was released Sunday (Oct. 25), riding in to AT&T Stadium and revealing the halftime performance news .

In a press statement also released on Sunday, Lambert adds, “There’s something special about how music brings people together, especially when it’s to spread joy and hope to families who need it most. The Salvation Army and the Dallas Cowboys have built an incredible tradition with the Red Kettle Kickoff, and I can’t wait to be back home in Texas this Thanksgiving to help carry it forward.”

Lambert’s Crisco album debuted at No. 4 on Billboard ’s Top Country Albums following its Oct. 2 release, continuing the singer’s unbroken run of 11 top 10s on the chart.

“The Red Kettle Kickoff has become one of the Dallas Cowboys’ proudest traditions and one my family and our entire organization look forward to every Thanksgiving,” says Charlotte Jones, chief brand officer/co-owner of the Dallas Cowboys and former national advisory board chairman for The Salvation Army. “For 30 years, incredible artists have appeared on our halftime stage to help The Salvation Army bring hope to millions of people in need. We’re grateful to Miranda Lambert for joining that legacy and helping us continue this meaningful tradition.”

Past performers to headline the team’s Thanksgiving game halftime show include the late Dolly Parton, who memorably came out on the stadium field in a Cowboys cheerleaders outfit in 2023. Reba McEntire was the inaugural star to headline the show in 1997. Over the years, Destiny’s Child, Carrie Underwood, the Jonas Brothers, Selena Gomez, Lainey Wilson and Post Malone were also among the artists leading the halftime entertainment for the Cowboys.
